key_insight: Generative AI blurs the line between original and appropriated ideas, making idea plagiarism harder to detect and requiring updated definitions and governance for research misconduct.
problem_solved: Clarifies the ethical and practical challenge of identifying and responding to plagiarism of ideas when GenAI tools can generate, remix, or obscure intellectual contributions and provenance.
method: Conceptual analysis of how GenAI alters idea provenance and the limits of current plagiarism frameworks.
Examination of detection and attribution challenges, plus illustrative case scenarios showing ambiguity in responsibility.
Policy-focused recommendations for redefining research misconduct and improving institutional practices around attribution and disclosure.
impact: Provides actionable framing for institutions, journals, and researchers to update policies and review practices, helping preserve trust, attribution, and accountability in AI-augmented research.
visual_elements: Flowchart showing idea generation pathways: human → human, human + GenAI → human, GenAI → human, with arrows indicating provenance uncertainty.
Venn diagram contrasting text plagiarism, idea plagiarism, and GenAI-assisted outputs to highlight overlaps and gaps in detection.
Checklist infographic for institutions: disclosure, provenance tracking, authorship criteria, and investigation steps.
Timeline or decision tree illustrating how an allegation of idea plagiarism would be assessed with/without GenAI involvement.
paper_title: Plagiarism of ideas in the age of generative artificial intelligence
